html:
SMTO-HTTP-0060 — The Agent used a connection that isn't open in this Run

GUID: 875336b9-3f6a-4556-983b-a9b4dfd6ce6d
Slug: http-connection-ref-not-current
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Agent pointed its web request at a connection this Run doesn't have open; it may be from an earlier Run or simply wrong. SMTO stopped the request, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the Agent to continue. SMTO tells it which connections are open and lets it correct itself up to two times. The Agent can usually switch to the right connection without your help.
  2. If the Run stops, reply in the Conversation asking the Agent to connect to the service again and use that connection for the request. A fresh connection gives the Agent a reference that is valid in this Run.
  3. If the service uses a saved connection, tell the Agent its name as shown in Parameter Store. Naming the saved connection removes any guesswork about which one to use.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's next web request goes through and its result appears in the Conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Nothing was sent to the other service, so you don't need to check it for changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • While verified HTTP reuse was active, http.request supplied a connection_ref that is not a string naming one of this run's current established connections, so the routing.http_reuse guard rejected it without dispatch.

What this means

  • A supplied connection_ref is not a string naming one of this run's current established connections while verified HTTP reuse is active. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A supplied connection_ref is not a string naming one of this run's current established connections while verified HTTP reuse is active.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the literal reference with current connection discovery, never with a guessed or historical ID.

How to fix it

  • Use a connection_ref returned by an http.connect in the current run, or the verified profile_key; references from earlier runs, other Gateways or invented values are rejected. The model gets two correction attempts before the run is blocked with http_reuse_correction_limit; check conversation.reuse_corrected and http.connection_ref_rejected events.
  • Refresh connection discovery and use the returned current reference for the intended origin. Do not fabricate or reuse a stale reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected current reference resolves under normal origin, profile and permission checks.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
